title: Scouting Jets UDFA edge defender Nathan Voorhis
summary: Over the last few months, we’ve been breaking down all undrafted free agents signed by the Jets. We continue today with former Ball State edge defender Nathan Voorhis. The 24-year old Voorhis is listed at 6’2” and 251 pounds and was a first-team all-MAC selection last year as he racked up 12 sacks for Ball […]
full_text: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - AUGUST 30: Ball State University defensive end Nathan Voorhis (44) sacks Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne (15) during the college football game between the Purdue Boilermakers and Ball State Cardinals on August 30, 2025, at Ross-Ade Stadium in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the last few months, we’ve been breaking down all undrafted free agents signed by the Jets. We continue today with former Ball State edge defender Nathan Voorhis. The 24-year old Voorhis is listed at 6’2” and 251 pounds and was a first-team all-MAC selection last year as he racked up 12 sacks for Ball State. He had also played for Bryant College and UConn during his career. Background Voorhis was a three-star high school recruit, having played defensive end and tight end. He headed to UConn in 2022, but struggled to earn any playing time in two years with the Huskies. He had seven tackles and played just 20 defensive snaps. Having opted to transfer to Bryant College in 2024, Voorhis started four games and ended up with 47 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and five sacks in 11 games. This earned him the opportunity to transfer back to a top-level school and he broke out with 12 sacks in his only season at Ball State. He also had 51 tackles, 17 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles in 12 games. Having not been invited to the scouting combine, Voorhis’ pro day numbers were a mixed bag and he ultimately didn’t get drafted in April. Voorhis was one of the first round of undrafted free agents signed by the Jets and his contract reportedly includes $70K of guaranteed money. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Voorhis brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Voorhis doesn’t have ideal size and length, or an outstanding athletic profile, although he shows flashes of strength and explosiveness on film and did post a 37-inch vertical at his pro day. His agility numbers were poor and he ran a 4.76 in the 40-yard dash and posted 22 bench press reps, which are about average for his size. Usage Voorhis played as an edge throughout his college career, lining up inside on an occasional basis and playing both with his hands in the dirt or standing up. Motor Voorhis showcases a good motor on film as he battles in the trenches and relentlessly tries to get after the quarterback even when initially blocked. He played 50 or more snaps in eight of 12 games in 2025, with a highest snap count of 62 so he can handle a large workload. Pass rush Voorhis didn’t get a chance to show what he could do as a pass rusher at UConn and when he dropped down to the FCS level, he had five sacks but his pressure rate wasn’t that impressive. However, he broke out immediately at Ball State. After five games, he was leading the nation with eight sacks, including 3.5 against Ohio. He ended the year with 12 in 12 games. Only four players had more, including his new teammate David Bailey, who had 14.5 in 14. Voorhis has the ability to get around the edge, and displays good bend and burst coming around the corner. He is less effective on the bull rush, using that more as a set up for other moves, but does possess the power to move his man off his spot. Run defense Voorhis isn’t known for his run defense and his lack of size often leads to analysts suggesting he will probably be a situational rusher at the pro level. However, his performance grades on sites such as Pro Football Focus have typically been good. As you’d expect, his burst and motor on the edge can be an asset when he is employed in backside pursuit. There were times where he tried to penetrate and got sealed off but he has shown some ability to execute edge-setting assignments. Technique By the time he arrived at Ball State, Voorhis had developed an impressive collection of pass rush moves and shows an instinctive ability to transition from one to another. When rushing outside, he tends to set up his move by leaning to the inside and then when he comes around the corner, he rips through effectively. He displays good timing with his hands, and brings some aggression when chopping an offensive lineman’s arm away and can employ a hump/club move effectively when stunting inside. He impressively takes advantage of the offensive lineman here, using a bull-jerk move to get him off balance. Special teams Voorhis got plenty of special teams experience during his college career, especially at UConn, where he had seven special teams tackles in two seasons. He also saw time rushing kicks and punts and served as a blocker on the kick return unit. Tackling Voorhis was a relatively productive tackler over the past two years, but did miss tackles from time to time, including seven last season. He had three forced fumbles in his college career. Coverage Voorhis rarely dropped into coverage and never batted down a pass at the line during his college career. Instincts/Intelligence As noted, Voorhis is an instinctive pass rusher and he doesn’t seem to make many mental errors. On this play, he isn’t fooled on the option keeper. He jumped offside once last season. Attitude/Demeanor Voorhis impressed his coaches at Ball State with how quickly he adjusted to his new team and embraced a leadership role. He said he enjoyed the family-like environment they had created. His on-field discipline was solid with just five penalties in his career, although he did have a personal foul for roughing the passer last season. Injuries Voorhis played in 44 games in four seasons and doesn’t appear to have had any injuries during his college career. Scheme Fit As noted, Voorhis is widely viewed as a potential situational rusher but the Jets already have Bailey and Will McDonald, who also might be employed in such a role. In preseason, you can expect him to have a conventional edge role with the third unit but he should get plenty of opportunities to show what he can do against lower level opponents. Current Jets edge defender Eric Watts was one of Voorhis’ teammates at UConn. Conclusions The Jets don’t have a great deal of depth at the edge positions, nor do they have much of a pipeline in terms of developmental projects at the position. Therefore, it’s a good opportunity for a player like Voorhis to stick around if he can flash a few times in preseason. He should be looking at players like Watts, Braiden McGregor and Tyler Baron as being ahead of him but viable targets for him to try and outproduce in preseason. That would give him a good chance of a practice squad spot and potentially some playing time before the year is out.

summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL All-Breakout Team, Defense: Abdul Carter, Jihaad Campbell, Travis Hunter poised for big Year 2 – NFL.comJIHAAD CAMPBELL — After serving an apprenticeship under Nakobe Dean during his rookie season, Campbell is ready to take the full-time reins as Philadelphia’s man in the middle […]
full_text: Jun 10, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jihaad Campbell (30) shadow boxes during minicamp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL All-Breakout Team, Defense: Abdul Carter, Jihaad Campbell, Travis Hunter poised for big Year 2 – NFL.com JIHAAD CAMPBELL — After serving an apprenticeship under Nakobe Dean during his rookie season, Campbell is ready to take the full-time reins as Philadelphia’s man in the middle following Dean’s free-agent departure to Las Vegas. The athletic linebacker will enhance defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s scheme with his length and range. Moreover, he will add a new dimension to the Eagles’ defense with his playmaking ability at the second level, shining as a run-and-chase defender with pass-rush ability. With the former first-rounder installed in a premium position in Fangio’s D, Campbell could quickly emerge as a star in his second season. The 2026 Eagles are taking “connection” seriously – BGN “Tough. Detailed. Together.” Since Nick Sirianni was hired as the head coach of the Philadelphia Eagles in 2021, he has doubled down on his core values for the team, with connection being one of the most prominent staples. He’s prioritized this in many ways over the years, but heading in the 2026 season, we’re seeing more of the relationship building that’s happening behind the scenes and ahead of training camp. Not that these opportunities to connect as teammates and friends haven’t existed in the past, but there has seemingly been more cameras around to capture it this year. Whatever your opinion on football players posting their workouts, during a long offseason, it at least gives fans a little hope that the team is focused and building a solid foundation in their time away from the building. If nothing else, the 2026 Eagles roster should be as close as ever as they embark on (another) season with high expectations. NFL fans predict the NFC division winners – SB Nation Eagles overwhelming NFC East favorites. We started our tour of the NFC in the East, where the Philadelphia Eagles were tapped as overwhelming favorites to win the division. Of those who responded, 67% picked Philadelphia to win the division, followed by the Dallas Cowboys with 15%, and the New York Giants with 13%. Washington rounded out the results with 5%. You can see the results, and the full discussion that followed, here. Why Nick Sirianni isn’t concerned handing the keys to inexperienced OC – NBCSP Sirianni likes that story so much because it shows just how hard of a worker Mannion is; how bad he wants it. Sirianni also said that during the spring, there wasn’t a day he beat Mannion to the Jefferson Health Training Complex and there wasn’t a day where Mannion’s car wasn’t still in the parking lot when he left. That work ethic at least partially explains why the Eagles feel like Mannion is ready to be an offensive coordinator in just his third season as a coach at any level. “This dude loves football and he loves to work,” Sirianni said. “I mean I’ve really enjoyed being around him and just his desire. Sometimes we think ‘man he’s talented’ about everybody, ‘man he’s just got it.’ But it doesn’t happen without, whether it’s a player, whether it’s Sean, it doesn’t happen without just this obsession to get better. Assistant coaches who could break out in 2026 for all 32 NFL teams – The Athletic Philadelphia Eagles: Joe Kasper, defensive pass game coordinator. If a young assistant coach can stick around — and even thrive — under top defensive mind Vic Fangio, he is often destined for bigger things. Kasper has worked for Fangio in both Miami and Philadelphia, and is poised for a bigger role now that former colleague Christian Parker (another Fangio disciple) is in Dallas. Nguyen, our senior writer, noted that the “two-high trend will continue to grow and it seems like coaches that can successfully implement some of Fangio’s ideas into their systems take it to another level.” High expectations also surround first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, who is expected to bring elements of Matt LaFleur’s Green Bay/Shanahan-derived system to Philadelphia. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Fantasy Preview: Can Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley bounce back? – NBC Sports 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Win Total. DraftKings Over/Under: 10.5. Pick: Under (-140). In my heart, I want to pick the over, but -140 for the under is a better price than you can find at most books. It’s easy to see why books think the Eagles aren’t likely to hit 11 wins. They lost several starters in free agency and drafted for the future. Makai Lemon isn’t going to fully replace A.J. Brown as a rookie and none of their subsequent picks are projected to start in 2026. Howie Roseman sacrificed some short-term win probability to build a better team in the long run, and that is enough to convince me to take the value on the under. Eagles 2026 Training Camp Position Preview: Special Teams – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Kicker Jake Elliott enters his 10th season of his storied career with the Eagles. The Illinois native is second all-time in career points for the Eagles (1,007), only behind David Akers (1,323). Elliott owns the record for most 50+ yard field goals (33) in team history. In Super Bowl LIX, he broke the record for most points in a Super Bowl by a kicker with 15, passing 1968 Don Chandler. The 2023 second-team All-Pro ended 2025 with 100% accuracy on field goals on the 39-yard line or closer. On extra points, Elliott had a 97.6% success rate in 2025. The Memphis product did something he had never done in his career in 2025 – record a special teams tackle. [BLG Note: I get that the team’s official website isn’t going to be super critical of Elliott but to not even make the slightest mention of his struggles the past two seasons is kinda wild.] After Asking Steelers For New Home, Kenny Pickett ‘Begged’ Eagles To Trade Him, Says His College Coach – Steelers Depot “The Eagles did not want to trade him,” Narduzzi said recently on 99.9 The Fan’s YouTube channel. “He begged to be traded because he wanted to compete and he felt like he wasn’t going to have a chance to beat out Jalen Hurts. I think there’s some misconceptions about, ‘They just got rid of him.’ No. They wanted him to stay, and they said, ‘We’re not trading you.’ And he begged, and they said, ‘If it’s good for us, we’ll trade you. But if it’s not good for us, we’re not making that move.’” Decoding Jonathan Gannon’s Eagles Defense: What the Coverage Data Reveals – Acme Packing Company Taken together, the data supports a more nuanced read of Gannon than either side of the public debate about him usually allows. He wasn’t simply “too passive,” as some critics argued throughout 2022 — the third-down man-coverage rates and the spikes in blitz aggression in specific weeks show a coordinator capable of asking his defense to take risks when the situation called for it. But he also wasn’t a chess master constantly innovating new wrinkles — the season-long drift toward zone and away from blitzing suggests a defense settling into its most repeatable, lowest-variance version of itself as the year went on, trusting disciplined execution of a smaller menu of calls over an expanding one. How much Cowboys failure belongs to Dak Prescott – Blogging The Boys But he has. That’s because there is another option that remains, and that is for Prescott to be the thing that is elevated. That is not a crazy expectation. Dak is compensated heavily, and it is totally fair to expect a player who commands that type of team resources to make a bigger impact. He has to, at some point, be the guy who punishes aggressive defensive attacks instead of falling victim to them. When the clock is running down, he has to make that throw. He has to be that guy. While Prescott is by no means the problem in Dallas, he has not been the…

Saquon Barkley and Cooper DeJean working on their speed and agility in this summer heat 🔥 We are so back 🦅 Is that Ringo I see 👀 pic.twitter.com/SWFiVI6jHI — Cooper DeJAWN 🦅 (@CooperDeJawn3) July 14, 2026 We’ve seen Jalen Hurts hosting the entire QB room, and most of the team’s wide receivers and tight ends for a combination of on-field work and off-field bonding earlier in the summer, but it’s also really cool to see Eagles players from both the offense and defense finding ways to train together in the offseason. The Eagles DB room has also been working a lot the past few weeks with different combinations of corners and safeties, new guys and players returning to Vic Fangio’s defense. Eagles safeties Andrew Mukuba, Marcus Epps, Andre’ Sam and Kapena Gushiken are training together with @Dkgamble in California. 👀 (🎥: dgambletrainingofficial on Instagram) pic.twitter.com/dNIXkk9Qve — Anthony DiBona (@DiBonaNFL) July 1, 2026 Offszn DB work…the countdown to Camp!! 🎥 @ReaperactionJ IG reaperaction_jay_media @DiBonaNFL @tomstakes pic.twitter.com/puLlyIyAtw — Reaperaction_jay (@ReaperactionJ) July 7, 2026 There have been many opportunities for some of the new guys to build chemistry with their teammates, and to forge a deeper connection with guys they’ve played with for years. Nothing highlights that last piece quite as much as Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith spending significant time together this offseason. That’s not entirely surprising given their long history and strong friendship, but both players seem even more committed to raising the bar this season. The pair trained together at Temple University, participated in a flag football game — as did Barkley, but the RB was on the opposing team —, and off the field, Hurts supported Smith at his charity softball game and at the WR’s wedding. With A.J. Brown now in New England, everyone, including Hurts and Smith, knows how important their connection is going to be this season. There’s also been a ton of support among teammates at their various charity endeavors the past few months. Smith’s softball game always draws several Eagles to the mound, there have been more than a few golf events that many participated in, and the Eagles Autism Challenge was another huge success. Bottom line, if a player was doing something positive for the community, at least one of his teammates was there to show support. It’s not just the players who are putting in work to connect this offseason, either. There are a lot of new faces throughout the coaching staff, and Sirianni has been working on bringing everyone together, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic . “Sirianni focused on team and staff bonding events this offseason. There was a team dinner and bowling outing. They played basketball at Saint Joseph’s University. On the last day of training camp, there was a cookout for families. Sirianni had a get-together with all the coaches at a Philadelphia establishment. Mannion hosted the offensive coaches at a separate event and invited Sirianni and his wife. This concept is not totally original, and similar stories from previous summers that take Sirianni’s temperature ahead of training camp would include comparable examples. These, too, are Sirianni’s greatest hits.” We’re still quite far from knowing exactly what kind of expectations are realistic for the upcoming season, but it’s encouraging to see everyone putting in work on their own time and trying to improve the standard for the locker room culture.

title: Eagles schedule preview: Cowboys
summary: When and where: Week 7 at home on Monday Night Football; Week 12 in Dallas for Thanksgiving Key additions: DC Christian Parker, S Jalen Thompson, EDGE Rashan Gary, LB Dee Winters, CB Cobie Durant Key subtractions: DC Matt Eberflus, DT Osa Odighizuwa, S Kenneth Murray, LB Donovan Wilson Last season: For the first time since […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on prior to a game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images When and where: Week 7 at home on Monday Night Football; Week 12 in Dallas for Thanksgiving Key additions: DC Christian Parker, S Jalen Thompson, EDGE Rashan Gary, LB Dee Winters, CB Cobie Durant Key subtractions: DC Matt Eberflus, DT Osa Odighizuwa, S Kenneth Murray, LB Donovan Wilson Last season: For the first time since 1969, a Cowboys game ended in a tie The question for this team: Can the defense get out of its own way? I would like to apologize to Brian Schottenheimer. Last year I said he was the Dave Campo of Jason Garretts. I was wrong. Brian Schottenheimer is the Jason Garrett of Wade Phillipses. The Cowboys were entertainingly mediocre last year. They scored 37 or more points four times. Only the Rams gained more yards, and only 43 more, which is a Brandon Aubrey chip shot. Half their games were one score games; and their prime time games were either close, high scoring, or both. The 2025 Cowboys were built to do one thing: move down the field almost at will and score a bunch of points. They did that. Actually they were built to do something else too: let the other team move the ball at will and score a bunch of points. And that they did. The Cowboys also gave up 37 or more points four times. They had the 3rd most yards given up. This meant that half their games were either close, high scoring, or both. Are you not entertained? That’s what Jerry Jones cares about. And the 2025 Cowboys were entertaining. They didn’t keep the excitement to the field, the Micah Parsons trade was a treat for the haters. What they were not was good. 7-9-1 wouldn’t have even won the NFC South, and the worst scoring defense in 2025 meant they did things like lose to the Cardinals, give up 3 TDs to Russell Wilson, and let JJ McCarthy look like a somewhat functioning QB. For all the production the offense had, they went 1-7-1 when the defense gave up more than 28 points, and that win was against the Russell Wilson led Giants in overtime. Yes, it is hard to win when your defense can’t stop anyone, but the point here is 1) the Cowboys defense gave up over 28 points in half their games and 2) the high powered offense couldn’t get the job done when it mattered most. The Cowboys beat up on bad teams: 44 points against the Commanders, 40 against the Giants, 37 against the Jets, 33 against the Raiders, but they also played terribly against some bad defenses: 14 points against the Bears, and 17 against the Giants and Cardinals. And yet, this team might win the division. It is not saying much to say that the defense has improved, but it has, with at least five new starters and a half a dozen new faces in rotation roles, and they have a new set of coaches. Good they will not be, but “not horrible” is a step up. This is far from a Super Bowl contending team, but a team with a good QB, a really good pair of WRs, a running game and a defense that isn’t tripping over itself is a team that can win double digit games.

title: Eagles News: Nick Sirianni using AI to help prepare for the 2026 season
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … For Nick Sirianni, AI offers fresh material entering another pivotal Eagles season – The AthleticNick Sirianni discovered ChatGPT this offseason. It’s his sixth season as the Philadelphia Eagles’ head coach, now longer than any stop in his NFL coaching career, and the stories are beginning […]
full_text: Jun 9, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni speaks with the media before a Minicamp session at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … For Nick Sirianni, AI offers fresh material entering another pivotal Eagles season – The Athletic Nick Sirianni discovered ChatGPT this offseason. It’s his sixth season as the Philadelphia Eagles’ head coach, now longer than any stop in his NFL coaching career, and the stories are beginning to repeat themselves. How many times can he preach his “tough, detailed, together” mantra before it feels like a rock star playing the greatest hits on tour? That’s why Sirianni logged into the artificial intelligence chatbot on a Monday in June — a program he knew so little about that he couldn’t get the name right — and began his research with a prompt: “Give me a great relentless effort true sports story.”This rabbit hole is how Sirianni learned about Anthony Robles, an Arizona State wrestler born with one leg who won a national championship in 2011. Sirianni planned to incorporate the anecdote into a speech to the team, a way to tell an old message in a new way. […] “We’ve created stories, things that people are looking up on ChatGP — fill me in on the letters,” Sirianni said in June during a roundtable interview. “What keeps it more fresh than what we’ve done?” Or what they’re about to do. That seems to be at the crux of Sirianni in Year 6, with the Eagles reporting to training camp on July 28. Spadaro: Nick Sirianni reveals the secret to team success – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Nick Sirianni is in a relaxed state of mind as his Philadelphia Eagles wrap up their offseason program. He is in the Jefferson Health Training Complex auditorium answering questions from reporters who cover the team every day, who have been dug in with the Eagles for each of Sirianni’s five seasons here. Sirianni’s core, what he’s all about and what he cares about the most, is the requested topic here: How to win big in the NFL. How to win it all. Sirianni has won big – postseason appearances in each of his five seasons – and he has won it all – an NFC Championship in the 2022 season and a win in Super Bowl LIX in the 2024 campaign – and he knows the most important component and it is the piece that he works on every … single … day. “How do you come together as a team? You come together as a football team through shared hardships. So, you get that, right, through the offseason,” Sirianni said, gaining passion. “You come together as a football team through building trust of consistently doing what you’re supposed to do. Consistently on a daily basis. And you come together as a football team through the time that you put in with each other. And that time, sometimes it feels like it’s invisible progress. It’s like, am I really making progress here, but you have to keep putting it in, knowing that at some point it’s going to show itself up. Guys are working really, really, really hard to come together as a team because we know how important that is at the end of the day.” Nick Sirianni’s ability to adapt again will be put to the test in year six with the Eagles – Inquirer Flights were canceled, which meant new Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, a few weeks into the job and prior to his family making its move east, was facing a delay returning to the office. It was a few days into free agency, and NFL draft prep was in full swing. Mannion could have picked up the phone and called his new boss, Nick Sirianni, to tell him his return trip to Philadelphia would be delayed. Instead, he got in the car and started driving the 900-plus mile route to his new home. Sirianni called his new offensive coordinator to check in and was surprised to learn that Mannion was five hours away. “This dude loves football and he loves to work,” Sirianni said last month during an extended interview session with Eagles beat reporters. “I’ve really enjoyed being around him. “I think we think — about everybody — ‘Man, he’s just got it.’ But it doesn’t happen — whether it’s a player, whether it’s Sean — without this obsession to get better. Sean has this obsession to get better, this obsession with his craft, which is why he’s excelled in this profession and I’m really looking forward to continuing to work with him.” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni: DeVonta Smith is ‘capable of doing even more’ – PHLY There has been a palpable enthusiasm surrounding DeVonta Smith stepping into a more featured role than he already occupied in the Eagles offense as a result of the departure of A.J. Brown this offseason, and Sirianni suggested as much a few days after Brown was traded to the New England Patriots back in June. “DeVonta, he’s a special player that can continue to get even more targets than he has,” Sirianni said. “He’s so capable of doing even more. And he’s just such a good football player.” As I wrote earlier this offseason, there’s internal belief that Smith could be among the league’s most productive receivers if he creeps closer to the 150-target mark that the likes of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua surpassed in their respective offenses last season. Smith finished last year with 113 targets, 77 catches and 1,008 receiving yards. He had a career-high 136 targets in 2022 and caught 95 of them for 1,196 receiving yards. But his yards per route run in 2025 might be the most instructive when assessing the Eagles’ case for optimism. On the 51 routes he ran with Brown off the field last year (admittedly a small sample size), his 2.67 yards/route run ranked fourth in the NFL among qualifying receivers. Everybody loves new Eagles CB Riq Woolen – PhillyVoice Nick Sirianni doesn’t typically like singling out players for playing well in practices, but he made a rare exception for one in an interview ahead of Eagles training camp. “There are so many guys working their asses off that I never want to be like, ‘Oh, this guy looks good, and I didn’t mention this guy.’ But Riq Woolen, I’m really excited to have him,” Sirianni said. “And I feel like every day I’m like, ‘Wow, that was an impressive play.’ “We can get so caught up in wow plays. What wins is consistency. But the wow plays are fun to watch. And like, he has a lot of wow plays and he is consistent. He’s being consistent with that. And so I’m really, really looking forward to him and Quinyon and Coop kind of roaming back there. “And Riq works his butt off, and you’re not supposed to look like that when you play corner. Like he just looks the part. I have these guys throughout the NFL of like, ‘Hey that dude didn’t look real.’ You look at somebody like – I remember I used to think that way when I saw Calvin Johnson as a receiver. I always thought that of Julio Jones. You ain’t supposed to look like that. And I feel like that with Riq. Like, you ain’t supposed to look like that at that position. He’s freaky. And yeah, excited about that.” Eagles schedule preview: Panthers – BGN The 2025 Panthers were not really interested in actually trying to play football. The 2026 team doesn’t seem to be either. Tet McMillian was the only Panther with more than 400 receiving yards, Carolina’s biggest additions to their WR room were John Metchie and his 686 career yards, and a Josh Heupel WR. Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips (when he’s healthy) should improve the defense, but this is an offense that scored fewer than 14 points seven times last year. You’d need the 1985 Bears defense to win with that kind of output. While the Panthers did pick up Bryce Young’s fifth year option, putting him under contract for 2027 for a guaranteed $26M, they are–correctly–not expected to sign him to a contract extension this offseason. Changes – Iggles Blitz Handling change goes beyond the GM. It takes a whole organizational commitment. You need the college scouting staff to find young talent to replenish the…

(Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. had what many would consider a breakout season in 2025. The defensive back posted a career-high 14 passes defended in 2025, and cut his penalty numbers back from a league-leading 17 in 2024 to just nine. However, many believe Porter Jr. is set to take another massive leap this season. Bradley Locker of Pro Football Focus listed 10 players that could make the jump to earning their first All-Pro in 2026, with Porter Jr. being one of those listed. 10 players capable of making their first All-Pro team in 2026👀 pic.twitter.com/LLgQf4aK0V — PFF (@PFF) July 17, 2026 “Porter already looked dominant on a defense that finished near league average in passing success rate, plus 21st in PFF coverage grade. Those metrics figure to augment in 2026 with Pittsburgh signing impressive corner Jamel Dean and hiring Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator,” Locker wrote. “The 25-year-old Porter has the combination of length, physicality and bravado to take another step this season.” According to PFF, the 32nd overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft ranked in the 90th percentile in coverage grade last season. He also ranked in the 91st percentile in single coverage, while ranking among the best in the 96th percentile in forced incompletion rate last season. Porter Jr. is eligible for a massive contract extension that could pay him upwards of $30 million per season. summary: Welcome to Part II of our countdown of the 30 greatest Pittsburgh Steelers of all time. full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 18: Wide Receiver Antonio Brown #84 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates after a catch during the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at TIAA Bank Field on November 18, 2018 in Jacksonville, Florida. Steelers defeated the Jaguars 20 to 16. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Part II of our countdown of the 30 greatest Pittsburgh Steelers of all time. Part I featured multiple Hall of Fame players from multiple eras, as well as legends from before the Steelers became one of the blue blood franchises of the NFL. Today, four wide receivers and five Hall of Famers highlight No. 20-11 on our countdown. Meet the panel Jarrett Bailey, SB Nation Chris Carter, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette Don Chedrick, 93.7 The Fan Dave Dameshek, Meadowlark Media Todd Haley, Former Steelers Offensive Coordinator Tommy Jaggi, FanSided Alan Saunders, Steelers Now Joe Starkey, 93.7 The Fan 20. Donnie Shell Career stats Interceptions: 51 Forced fumbles: 12 Fumble recoveries: 19 Career accolades 5-time Pro Bowler 4-time All-Pro 3-time First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion Pro Football Hall of Fame (2020) Player tribute From undrafted to the Hall of Fame, Donnie Shell was another key cog in the Steelers’ defenses of the 1970s. He plays in north of 200 games, earned a handful of Pro Bowls (when they still meant something) and multiple All-Pros sprinkled in, as well. – Don Chedrick 19. Cam Heyward Career stats Tackles: 796 Tackles for loss: 142 Sacks: 92 Forced fumbles: 9 Fumble recoveries: 7 Pass deflections: 64 Career accolades 7-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro 4-time First-Team All-Pro 2023 Walter Payton Man of the Year Player tribute Few players in the history of the NFL have aged as gracefully as Cam Heyward. He’s been selected to six All-Pro teams in his career – two came after his 35th birthday. He enters the 2026 season just eight sacks away from joining the 100 sack club, despite being an interior defensive lineman – an incredible feat to reach. He will walk into the Hall of Fame once he is first eligible, but judging by the fact that he is under contract through the 2027 season, that resume will be even greater when the time comes. – Jarrett Bailey 18. Hines Ward Career stats Receptions: 1,000 Yards: 12,083 Touchdowns: 85 Career accolades 4-time Pro Bowler 3-time All-Pro (All Second-Team) 2-time Super Bowl champion Super Bowl XL MVP Player tribute Hines Ward wasn’t the prototypical wide receiver of his era. While names like Marvin Harrison, Andre Johnson, and Chad Johnson helping innovate the game with aerial attacks all over the NFL, Ward was the gritty, hard-nosed receiver that did the dirty work while still being able to take the top off of defenses. Ward was a Pro Bowler from 2001-04 and recorded 90+ receptions each season from 2001-03. He’s one of the best receivers of his era, and is the franchise’s all-time leader in receptions. – Jarrett Bailey 17. James Harrison Career stats Tackles: 811 Tackles for loss: 128 Sacks: 84.5 Interceptions: 8 Forced fumbles: 34 Fumble recoveries: 9 Career accolades 5-time Pro Bowler 4-time All-Pro 2-time First-Team All-Pro 2-time Super Bowl champion 2008 Defensive Player of the Year Player tribute One of the scariest players to ever don a Steelers uniform. Short in stature, Harrison waited years for his chance to be a starter. That chance finally came in 2007 when Mike Tomlin took over as head coach. He was a Pro Bowler and Second-Team All-Pro in his first season in a starting role and won Defensive Player of the Year in 2008. He capped off that season with what is, for my money, the greatest defensive play in Super Bowl history. – Don Chedrick 16. Lynn Swann Career stats Receptions: 336 Yards: 5,462 Touchdowns: 51 Career accolades 3-time Pro Bowler 3-time All-Pro 1978 First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion Super Bowl X MVP 1970s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (2001) Player tribute Swann was often stereotyped as soft due to taking ballet lessons, but the future made a living out of getting up from big hits and making big catch after big catch in the biggest moments. His pair of memorable catches against the Dallas Cowboys in Super Bowl X secured him MVP honors, and he was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2001. – Jarrett Bailey 15. T.J. Watt Career stats Tackles: 354 Tackles for loss: 136 Sacks: 115 Interceptions: 9 Forced Fumbles: 36 Fumble recoveries: 14 Career accolades 8-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro 4-time First-Team All-Pro 3-time sack leader 2021 Defensive Player of the Year Player tribute When you have a brother that will be a first-ballot Hall of Famer, that comes with pressure. However, T.J. Watt has carved out a Hall of Fame legacy of his own. He is the only player in NFL history to lead the league in sacks three times, and his 2021 season is one of the best we’ve ever seen from a defensive player. – Jarrett Bailey 14. Antonio Brown Career stats Receptions: 928 Yards: 12,291 Touchdowns: 83 Career accolades 7-time Pro Bowler 5-time All-Pro 4-time First-Team All-Pro 2-time receptions leader 2-time receiving yards leader Super Bowl champion 2010s All-Decade Team Player tribute From the first day I met Antonio Brown, he had one goal that never changed – to be the best receiver in the NFL. And from 2012-17, he was that. No one practiced harder than AB, no one played harder than AB. To this day, he’s the hardest worker I’ve ever been around. – Todd Haley 13. John Stallworth Career stats Receptions: 537 Yards: 8,723 Touchdowns: 63 Career accolades 3-time Pro Bowler 2-time All-Pro 1979 First-Team All-Pro 4-time Super Bowl champion Pro Football Hall of Fame (2002) Player tribute While Lynn Swann drew a crowd thanks to his acrobatic ‘showstopper’ ability, John Stallworth was the cog in the Steelers’ passing game that kept the engine running. At 6’2” and 190 pounds, Stallworth was a complete wide receiver with size, route-running precision, and soft hands. Stallworth played all 14 NFL seasons in Pittsburgh, recording 537 receptions for 8,723 yards and 63 touchdowns. The 1979 First-Team All-Pro receiver and three-time Pro Bowler is third all-time in receiving yards and touchdowns for the Steelers. – Tommy Jaggi 12. Dermontti Dawson Career accolades 7-time Pro Bowler 6-time All-Pro (All First-Team) 1990s All-Decade Team Pro Football Hall of Fame (2012) Player tribute The Steelers were one of the best rushing offenses in the NFL throughout the 1990s, and Dawson was a big reason for that. The commander of Pittsburgh’s offensive line, Dawson helped spring Jerome Bettis to three seasons of 1,100+ yards, including 1,431 in 1996 and 1,665 in 1997. He was inducted into the the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2012. – Jarrett Bailey 11. Alan Faneca Career accolades 9-time Pro Bowler 8-time All-Pro 6-time First-Team All-Pro Super Bowl champion 2000s All-Decade team Pro Football Hall of Fame (2021) Player tribute It’s an accomplishment in and of itself when an NFL player can earn All-Pro honors. But to be considered arguably the best at your position for an extended period of time is a rare feat. This was the case for seven-time Pro Bowler and six-time First-Team All-Pro guard Alan Faneca. Faneca was inarguably the best offensive lineman in the Steelers’ second-most successful era in franchise history. The road-grading guard played a pivotal role in Super Bowl XL and was voted to the Associated Press’ 2000s All-Decade Team. – Tommy Jaggi Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Former Jets GM takes jab at Aaron Rodgers, Steelers
summary: There aren’t too many people within the NFL mediasphere that you’ll find picking the Pittsburgh Steelers to have a big season. This is despite the Steelers winning 10 games for the third consecutive year in 2025, winning the AFC North in the process, and adding a ton of talent on both sides of the ball. […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 12: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs on to the field prior to the NFL 2025 game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images There aren’t too many people within the NFL mediasphere that you’ll find picking the Pittsburgh Steelers to have a big season. This is despite the Steelers winning 10 games for the third consecutive year in 2025, winning the AFC North in the process, and adding a ton of talent on both sides of the ball. While the list of Steelers doubters is a long one, you can add former New York Jets general manager Mike Tannenbaum to the list. Speaking on SportsCenter , Tannenbaum proclaimed that there is no chance Aaron Rodgers is taking the Steelers to the Super Bowl. “The only way he’s going to LA is if he flies there,” Tannenbaum said, via Andrew Vasquez . “They are the third-best team in the division.” The Steelers will have the usual suspects to worry about in the AFC North. The Cincinnati Bengals made improvements to a defense that desperately needed them. The biggest question, as it has unfortunately become for Cincinnati, is will Joe Burrow stay healthy? He’s missed at least seven games in two of the last three seasons, including missing nine contests in 2025. Much like the Steelers, the Baltimore Ravens are heading into a new era under new head coach Jesse Minter. Lamar Jackson missed time in 2025 with injuries of his own. Will he be able to have a bounce back season? And will Derrick Henry lose a step after just under 1,600 yards? Even if both Cincinnati and Baltimore get a good bill of health from their respective quarterbacks, it would be easy to make the argument the Steelers have the best roster in the division. Pittsburgh will play Cincinnati in Weeks 3 and 10 and will play Baltimore twice in the final month of the season in Weeks 15 and 18. Let us know what you think in the comments . Now, John Schneider and Mike Macdonald are turning to the United Football League in hopes of finding depth to bolster their Super Bowl-winning roster. The team is reportedly bringing in former Louisville Kings cornerback Deantre Prince, according to NFL reporter Aaron Wilson . Prince played six games for the Kings, who took home the United Bowl, the UFL’s championship, in June. The 25-year-old totaled 11 tackles, five pass breakups and one interception. After the team’s first six games, Prince was let go by the Kings, despite being one of their top-rated players on defense. View this post on Instagram Prior to his time in the UFL, Prince was a fifth-round pick in 2024 by the Jacksonville Jaguars. In his 10 games with the Jags, he made eight tackles and defended one pass. Prince was targeted 13 times, allowing five completions for 80 yards and a touchdown. Out of Ole Miss, Prince starred in his senior season, racking up 36 tackles and one interception before he flashed his athletic ability at the combine by running a 4.38-second 40-yard dash time. The Seahawks aren’t the only NFL team expressing interest in the Ole Miss product, as Prince worked out with the Cleveland Browns in June. If he does make the Seahawks roster, he would join fellow SEC graduate and fifth-round corner from the 2024 draft, Nehemiah Pritchett.

title: How would you define a ‘successful’ season for the 49ers in 2026?
summary: Two of the most popular offseason phrases: “He’s in the best shape of his life!” “It’s Super Bowl or Bust this year!” Can you ignore former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel’s workout pictures? Can you acknowledge that the Niners can have a successful season without hoisting a Lombardi? They’re not a lock to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks shakes hands with Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers following a game at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The Seattle Seahawks defeated the San Francisco 49ers 13-3. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two of the most popular offseason phrases: “He’s in the best shape of his life!” “It’s Super Bowl or Bust this year!” Can you ignore former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel’s workout pictures? Can you acknowledge that the Niners can have a successful season without hoisting a Lombardi? They’re not a lock to make the playoffs by any means, but have the fourth-best odds in the NFC. Once you make the postseason, anything goes. There are question marks surrounding this team that are enough to prevent the 49ers from making a playoff run. There is also enough star power to pair with the coaching to cover that has been supplemented by depth, where another NFC Championship appearance wouldn’t be a surprise. That brings us to today’s question of the day: How would you define a ‘successful’ season for the 49ers in 2026? My answer: The 49ers appearing in another NFC Championship qualifies as a successful season in my eyes. Making the playoffs is a low bar when talking about the current iteration of this team. It took a season like 2024, when the team completely bottomed out, for the 49ers to miss the playoffs. Many pundits are penciling the Rams in to win the NFC West. It’ll only get worse if Aaron Donald comes out of retirement. But it’s not as much of a shoo-in as it seems. The head-to-head may not work out in the Niners’ favor because of Week 1, but Kyle Shanahan has always found a way to stay competitive, if not have the upper hand, against Sean McVay. Winning is hard. Winning a playoff game is even more difficult. The 2025 49ers accomplished that feat. Most of us can agree that they overachieved, all things considered. I’m acting as if the 49ers won’t earn the No. 1 seed and get a bye. Therefore, they’d need to win at least two games to make it to the NFC Championship. Realistically, they’d win a home game and a game on the road. That’s a successful season. And if they end up winning a third, it’d be the third chance for this team to win a Super Bowl — inevitably, against you know who. Of course the team wants to not only make but win a Super Bowl. That’s the goal every year. Attainable? It is. Far-fetched? Hardly. Conquering the NFC and beating three teams that will more than likely be three of the top teams in the NFL is the definition of a successful season. You’ve then put yourself in a position to win a Super Bowl. What does a successful season for the 49ers look like to you? You can share your comments in The Feed, the comment section below, or both.

title: 3 questions for the 49ers at QB: Can Brock Purdy avoid getting dinged up?
summary: July will shortly turn into August, and soon the San Francisco 49ers will be playing preseason games. But while the season is nearing, the 49ers aren’t without questions going into 2026.  Over the next few weeks, we will look at each position group and post three questions, whether they are questions that will be answered […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 07: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after his team's win in the NFL 2025 game between San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Amanda Loman/Getty Images) | Getty Images July will shortly turn into August, and soon the San Francisco 49ers will be playing preseason games. But while the season is nearing, the 49ers aren’t without questions going into 2026. Over the next few weeks, we will look at each position group and post three questions, whether they are questions that will be answered in August or during the season. First, we start with the quarterback position: Can Brock Purdy stay healthy? I wouldn’t say Brock Purdy has been injury-prone over his career; instead, he’s more prone to be dinged up. While the 26-year-old has suffered a wide variety of injuries, either the timing or the severity has prevented Purdy from missing too many games up until the 2025 season. An oblique injury in 2022 caused some concern entering a Thursday night game in Seattle, but Purdy toughed it out to help the 49ers beat the Seahawks. Several weeks later, he’d suffer the elbow injury that would knock him and the 49ers out of the NFC Championship Game in Philadelphia. Still, he wouldn’t miss any games the following season, with the offseason being used to recover. 2023 was relatively clean for Purdy, with the exception of a concussion finding him on the injury report prior to a Week 8 loss to the Bengals, capping a three-game losing streak. 2024 was the same as the year before, with a right shoulder injury being the only blip, causing Purdy to miss a drubbing at the hands of the Packers. Despite that wide range of injuries, Purdy had only missed three games due to injury entering the 2025 season. But then a turf toe injury cost Purdy half of the 2025 season, where Mac Jones entered and kept the 49ers afloat until Purdy returned in Week 11 and finished the season, nearly leading San Francisco to an NFC West crown. But can Purdy stay healthy for an entire season? He’s been able to mostly avoid serious injury, but can he keep the dings and damage that’s common in an NFL season to prevent his name from hitting the injury report? If Purdy stays healthy, can he take that next step? What does the next step even look like for Purdy? It feels as if he’s been floating around that middle tier of quarterback rankings that are oh so popular around this time of year. But how can Purdy find himself inside that top-10 quarterback list? The first step would be to keep the interceptions at a minimum. Purdy has thrown double-digit picks in each of his last three seasons, which is a concern considering he played just nine games last season. With his 10 interceptions in nine games, Purdy had a career-high 3.5 interception rate, the first time he’s been over three percent in his career. Since he made his debut in 2022, Purdy has the second-highest interception rate in the league (minimum 1,000 pass attempts): Mac Jones – 2.8 Purdy – 2.7 Joe Flacco – 2.6 Tua Tagovailoa – 2.5 Sam Darnold – 2.5 Geno Smith – 2.5 That list is a who’s who of interception-prone quarterbacks, but Purdy is likely the best quarterback on that list. If the interception rate can drop, Purdy can find himself in the very-good-to-potentially-elite tier of quarterbacks. Maybe a fully-healthy season will help Purdy take that step. Maybe even the 49ers revamped receiver room will help as well. But it feels like there’s room for improvement for Purdy, and ideally 2026 will be the year it all comes together for the quarterback. How will the 49ers handle Mac Jones? Let’s look at this question through a hypothetical lens. The trade deadline for the 2026 season lands on November 10. Let’s say the 49ers are 6-2 by the time the Week 10 deadline comes around and Purdy is not only healthy but playing the best ball of his career with no signs of stopping. Now let’s look around the league. The Vikings are 4-4, staying afloat in the NFC North behind their defense but with subpar quarterback play from either Kyler Murray or JJ McCarthy. Maybe the Falcons or Colts are playing well, but they are less than thrilled with their quarterback situations. Let’s just say one of those four teams has floated a second-round pick, maybe a third, for Jones to try to right the ship. With Jones on an expiring deal, do the 49ers bite, or do they retain possibly the best backup quarterback in the league as a break-glass-in-case-of-emergency option? I am just here to ask the questions, not answer them. We will see how it plays out over the next few months, but if something like the scenario above plays out, the 49ers will definitely have a decision to make.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 49ers stars vouch for return of former WR in free agency
summary: The San Francisco 49ers made a couple of moves at wide receiver this offseason, signing Mike Evans and Christian Kirk in free agency, while drafting De’Zhaun Stribling with their first pick of the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 33 overall. Those three additions provide much-needed depth and talent at wide receiver, where the 49ers struggled […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Deebo Samuel #1 of the Washington Commanders looks on against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers made a couple of moves at wide receiver this offseason, signing Mike Evans and Christian Kirk in free agency, while drafting De’Zhaun Stribling with their first pick of the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 33 overall. Those three additions provide much-needed depth and talent at wide receiver, where the 49ers struggled in 2025. Without Brandon Aiyuk and Deebo Samuel, the 49ers didn’t have a wideout top 650 receiving yards, as injuries and struggles on the field led the way. Evans gives the 49ers a proven No. 1 wide receiver who can win on the outside, although he comes with his own risks after the most injury-laden season of his career in 2025. He’ll be 33 this season, but has been highly productive when healthy and should be a good red-zone weapon. Kirk dealt with injuries as well in 2025, but is another proven weapon who can operate out of the slot and give the 49ers good depth alongside Evans and Ricky Pearsall. Stribling’s role as a rookie is unclear, but he worked well after the catch in college and gives the 49ers a big, fast receiver at 225 pounds. Still, could the 49ers add one more weapon to the room? Former 49ers star Deebo Samuel remains a free agent this offseason after his deal with the Washington Commanders expired, and he’s searching for a new home. Samuel, 30, caught 72 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns with the Commanders in 2025, while playing in 16 games. He didn’t see much usage as a runner, getting only 17 carries for 75 yards and a touchdown. Samuel’s average depth of target was quite low once again at 5.2 yards per target, but he did have some big games for the Commanders, especially early in the season. Could he be another player that returns to the 49ers on a one-year deal? Some of his former teammates vouched for a potential return this weekend. On one of Samuel’s recent Instagram posts, both George Kittle and Kyle Juszczyk commented, welcoming the wideout back to the Bay Area should he choose to return. “I have a guest house with your name on it,” Juszczyk wrote, with Kittle writing a similar remark: ‘I also have a guest house labeled ‘Deebo’s second home.’” Now, the 49ers have mentioned the desire to get younger and cheaper, but they’ve also added several veterans this offseason, including Evans, Kirk, linebacker Dre Greenlaw, and others, as they look to maximize their current championship window. Samuel could be another low-cost, one-year option that gives the 49ers more depth and reliability at wide receiver with a familiar face. The wideout should find a new home, should he choose, before the season starts, and there are many better situations for more playing time, including with the Commanders, who don’t have any proven options behind Terry McLaurin. But there are also options available back home.

title: Buccaneers Off-Season Position Review: Wide Receivers & Tight Ends
summary: As the offensive portion of our offseason review nears its end, we’ll examine the group with by far the most questions entering the season. The Bucs’ offense will likely live and die by the production of its receiving corps and, by extension, its chemistry with quarterback Baker Mayfield. Let’s dive right into it. “13” Reasons […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - June 02: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Wide Receiver Emeka Egbuka (2) goes thru drills during the Tampa Bay Buccaneers OTA workout on June 02, 2026 at the AdventHealth Training Center in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As the offensive portion of our offseason review nears its end, we’ll examine the group with by far the most questions entering the season. The Bucs’ offense will likely live and die by the production of its receiving corps and, by extension, its chemistry with quarterback Baker Mayfield. Let’s dive right into it. “13” Reasons Why the Bucs Might Struggle? It’s hard to keep dwelling on it, but it’s an immutably present question for the 2026 Buccaneers until toe meets leather. Their franchise icon and all-time best offensive player is gone, and he leaves behind a hole in the depth chart that’s not easily replaceable. Ability to consistently beat man coverage, excellent jump ball and highlight-reel catch skills, true explosive play potential — Mike Evans brough all of these qualities to the table for 12 seasons and 176 career games. Whether or not those strengths could be reliably counted on at this point in his career is a valid question, but it’s foolish to deny he is still an extremely useful player when healthy. Without him on the field, Tampa struggled severely with uncovering versus man coverage, so you can expect to see heavy doses of such until the new-look corps can show otherwise. So when looking at what it means to lose Evans, it’s just as much about how he won versus the simple stats. That will be the biggest puzzle the remaining pass catchers and new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson need to decode. Will the Real Egbuka Please Stand Up? Emeka Egbuka shocked everyone last year by: A.) being the Bucs’ first-round pick in the first place, and B.) producing prolifically in his first 8 professional games. Egbuka stepped right in for the absences of Godwin and Evans and showed immediate chemistry with Mayfield, playing like one of the best receivers in football during the first half. Before the bye week, in 8 games, Egbuka recorded 34 receptions for 562 yards and 5 touchdowns. He made eye-popping catches over big-name competition, created huge chunk plays, and generally looked like a polished pro. Then it all went…not as great. Egbuka’s stats in weeks 9-18 cratered along with the rest of the offense as teams figured out how to defend him. The rest of the unit struggling with injuries and efficiency did not help, but Egbuka very much looked like a rookie trying to do too much. he logged just 29 catches (on 64 targets!) for 376 yards and 1 touchdown. His catch rate finished at a concerningly low 49.6%. It’s not all doom and gloom, nor should it be. The tape Egbuka put up in the first 8 weeks of 2025 shows a player doing lots of things well, but it’s always about staying ahead of the competition, and that is extremely difficult. Egbuka is young (will be 24 in October), mature, and now possesses a full year’s experience of being asked to handle a huge load. With a new coordinator hopefully better equipped to handle playcalling duties, more reliability from players like Godwin and Jalen McMillan, and generally more consistency for the whole offense, Egbuka should be in a good spot to take another positive step forward in his development. Is Chris Godwin Still a Dude? If Egbuka’s Year 2 development isn’t the biggest question facing the current Bucs receiving corps, then Godwin’s relevancy is certainly 1b. It’s been a rough handful of years for Godwin, who’s been a high-end No. 2 option for the Bucs passing game when he’s healthy. Unfortunately, he’s dealt with long-term recoveries to both a torn ACL and broken leg, the latter of which largely robbed him of 2024 and 2025 (16 total games, 13 starts). Now 30 years old, can Godwin rebound from all the aforementioned adversity to still be a consistent threat? It seems likely he will return to his primary role as a slot demon, where he produced like a monster for several seasons prior to fibula fracture, so that should help matters. Even if he can be a present, consistent chain mover in short yardage and screen situations, that would help immensely to take the burden off names like Egbuka, McMillan and rookie Ted Hurst and keep their focus on more intermediate and downfield work. Will Tight End Matter…at All? The Bucs have been happy enough with Cade Otton as their TE1 that they re-signed him to a 3-year deal this off-season for middle-of-the-road money and declined to bring in any serious competition to his target share beyond Day 3 pick Bauer Sharp. Fans have their complaints about Otton, mostly related to losing a handle on the ball at inopportune times, but he’s been a generally reliable presence as a pass catcher and run blocker who has improved slowly but surely over the better part of 4 years. The question will now be, “Will Zac Robinson really use him?” As Atlanta’s offensive coordinator, Robinson deployed Kyle Pitts to great effect whenever the two rivals played (Pitts scored 3 of his 5 total TDs last year in one game against Tampa). Pitts set career-highs with 88 catches for 928 yards in 2025. That said, he’s generally produced modestly with numbers more in line with Otton in years prior — last year was more a product of the Falcons being absolutely barren at the receiver position. Even without Evans, the Bucs will give Robinson a passing arsenal he never had with Atlanta, so that might keep Otton down in the pecking order. But, Otton also has size (6-5, 247 pounds) that Tampa now lacks, so is it possible to see more Otton action down in the red zone? That will be an interesting wrinkle to monitor.
author: Mike Kiwak

title: PFF doesn’t know who the Titans’ WR1 is
summary: The Tennessee Titans worked hard to revamp the wide receiver position this offseason. They drafted Carnell Tate at No. 4 overall and also signed Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Everyone expects Tate and Robinson to be the Titans’ top two receivers for quarterback Cam Ward in 2026. Well, everyone […]
full_text: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley (0) makes a catch during organized team activities at Vanderbilt Health Football Center Friday, May 29, 2026. | DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans worked hard to revamp the wide receiver position this offseason . They drafted Carnell Tate at No. 4 overall and also signed Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year , $70 million contract in free agency. Everyone expects Tate and Robinson to be the Titans’ top two receivers for quarterback Cam Ward in 2026. Well, everyone but Pro Football Focus, apparently. PFF recently ranked all 32 starting wide receivers (WR1) in the league. For the Titans, they… chose Calvin Ridley and ranked him dead last at No. 32 overall. In what universe is Ridley still the Titans’ WR1 after the Tate and Robinson offseason acquisitions? “ Ridley’s 2025 season was cut short by injury, but he is expected to return as Tennessee’s top target in 2026 ,” Dalton Wasserman and Max Chadwick wrote . “ He recorded 1,000-yard seasons in both 2023 and 2024. Before the injury, Ridley was averaging a career-high 17.8 yards per reception, which ranked fourth among wide receivers with at least 30 targets last season. Flanked by free-agent addition Wan’Dale Robinson and first-round pick Carnell Tate, Ridley should see more favorable matchups on the outside in 2026 .” Wasserman and Chadwick are talented writers, but this feels like a whiff. A lack of knowledge surrounding the Titans by mainstream media members isn’t new for this fanbase. A 32-year-old Ridley coming off a serious injury won’t be the Titans’ WR1 in 2026. In fact, Ridley is likely competing for the WR3 role with both Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Ayomanor and Dike had impressive rookie seasons, and should be better as sophomores. Ayomanor is a bigger bodied outside receiver with blocking capabilities. Like Ridley, Dike is flexible enough to play multiple receiving positions, both inside and outside. Ridley won’t be handed reps by Brian Daboll. Expect Tate and Robinson to be the Titans’ preferred receivers.

summary: The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. In camp (6): Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, […]
full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) runs the ball against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first quarter at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. We’ll be previewing several position groups until then. The Titans have six running backs on the offseason roster. Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh decided against making major changes. In camp (6) : Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, Nicholas Singleton, Julius Chestnut, Kalel Mullings, Michael Carter. Biggest storyline: The Titans are essentially running it back with Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears. There have been some back-end changes but make no mistake, the rushing attack will go as far as Pollard and Spears are capable of carrying them. An improved passing offense, spearheaded by Cam Ward and Brian Daboll, could have a positive impact on the ground-and-pound approach. Most to prove: Spears is entering a contract year. He’s missed a handful of contests in consecutive seasons as lingering issues muted his impact across 2024 and 2025. Borgonzi didn’t draft Spears, and he appears unlikely to earn an extension in Tennessee. Breakout star: Will Spears stay healthy enough to possibly breakout or even have a career-best season? The fanbase is excited about sixth-round rookie Nicholas Singleton. Singleton displayed explosiveness and athleticism at Penn State. He may be the future for the Titans with both Pollard and Spears in contract years, but he’s unlikely to make a huge impact in 2026. Training camp competition: Pollard, Spears, and Singleton are guaranteed to make the 53-man roster. Will the Titans keep four running backs? If so, Julius Chestnut, Kalel Mullings, and Michael Carter are all competing for that potential role. Chestnut is a veteran back and proven special teamer. Mullings disappointed as a rookie, but also has special teams upside as a former linebacker. Carter previously played for Saleh and has the closest skill set to Spears, if the Titans need insurance there given his history of injuries.

title: Washington Commanders hidden gems: 3 secret superstars for the 2026 roster
summary: The 2024 Washington Commanders made the NFC Championship game for the first time since 1991, which is also the last time the franchise won a Super Bowl. The 55-23 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2024 conference title game was a heartbreaker, but expecting that to happen in the first place for a franchise […]
full_text: The 2024 Washington Commanders made the NFC Championship game for the first time since 1991, which is also the last time the franchise won a Super Bowl. The 55-23 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2024 conference title game was a heartbreaker, but expecting that to happen in the first place for a franchise that hadn’t even had a winning season since 2015? Well, Commanders fans could be forgiven for being happy with what they had and severely excited for the future. Unfortunately for the Commanders, every season tells its own story and, for the 2025 team, it was back to a harsher reality. This team inverted its previous 12-5 record to 5-12. The defense fell apart, dropping from 23rd to 28th in DVOA . The offense experienced a more drastic downturn, from sixth to 23rd . Jayden Daniels, who may have had the best rookie season any quarterback has ever had , missed 10 games with multiple injuries, and the coaching on both sides of the ball was more suspect than expected. Offseason turnaround was as severe as one might imagine. Offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury was replaced by former assistant quarterbacks coach David Blough and defensive coordinator Joe Whitt Jr. (who was stripped of play-calling duties at midseason in favor of head coach Dan Quinn) was replaced by former Minnesota Vikings defensive backs coach & pass game coordinator Daronte Jones. So now, the optimism is back! “I feel like this is an elevated group with a lot of versatility,” Quinn said at the owners meetings in March . “I like the speed that we added to the team and for me, the thing I love the most is the competition that comes with putting a good group together. When you look at some of our positions… man, that is going to be a battle. And the thing that comes from that is where everyone lifts up and goes. So, having the new players in the building, we’ve had a lot of the current guys, so I get to see them on a pretty regular basis, but having the new guys in for their days when they signed, I enjoyed that. Because after a tough end of season into January and February, to get some of these guys in here to see their enthusiasm doing it all together, that was really cool.” To take that cool into the new season, Quinn will need serious contributions from everyone on the roster — not just the obvious stars. So, here’s three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Commanders — one underrated veteran, one underrated free-agent signing, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: Safety Jeremy Reaves A primary reason the team replaced Whitt with Jones was the pass defense. Which was… well, let’s be diplomatic. It sucked. The 2025 Commanders allowed 350 completions on 540 attempts (64.8%) for 4,400 yards (8.1 YPA), 33 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and an opponent passer rating of 104.2, which was the NFL’s fifth-worst. Blown assignments were the norm as opposed to the exception, and the only guy in that secondary who seemed to be able to transcend it was safety Jeremy Reaves. In 2025, Reaves allowed 22 catches on 34 targets for 211 yards, 134 yards after the catch, one touchdown, one interception, seven pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 79.4. He also had 58 solo tackles, 18 stops, five tackles for loss, and three pressures on just eight pass-rushing snaps. The @Commanders ' secondary was a disaster in 2025. Except for safety Jeremy Reaves. Guy to watch in 2026. pic.twitter.com/mxwdszGmN5 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) July 14, 2026 The undrafted free agent out of South Alabama bounced around for a good long time. The Philadelphia Eagles signed him in 2018, but he didn’t make final cuts. Washington signed Reaves off the street, but bounced him off and on their practice squad over the next few years enough to give the guy whiplash. He didn’t make the final roster out of camp until 2022, and that was the year he made the Pro Bowl and First-Team All-Pro as a special teamer. The Commanders signed him to a two-year, $6 million deal in 2024, and bumped that up to a new one-year, $3.5 million deal in 2025. Based on Reaves’ development and how things might go with better coaching, this may be the last time he’ll be talking about smaller contracts. “I think the biggest thing for me is that the game has just slowed down so much, even in from last year to this year,” Reaves said in Aug. 2025. “I was coming off a knee injury, and everything was just kind of going really fast. I was trying to prove myself to a new staff and a new front office. And this year I just came in with the confidence that all I have to do is be me, and at the end of the day this is a game. I get to come out here and have fun every day and compete. And so, I’ve just been out here flying around, looking at the different things that offenses are showing formation-wise, split-wise — okay, who’s on the ball? Where are my deep threats when I’m at safety? “Just going out there and just trusting what I see. I think that’s the big thing with guys, they might see something, but they don’t necessarily trust what they’re seeing. You got the instincts for a reason, so you gotta use them.” Reaves has the instincts, and he’s learned how to use them. He’ll be a crucial part of the Commanders’ defensive turnaround, assuming everything clicks with the guys around him. Underrated free agent: EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson The 2025 Commanders did get to the quarterback at a pretty decent rate; their 42 regular-season quarterback takedowns were slightly above league average . But their pressure rate of 19.6% was the NFL’s seventh-lowest, and the front office went after that problem with gusto in the offseason. They signed former Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Odafe Oweh to a four-year, $96 million contract with $68 million guaranteed. They also penned former New England Patriots edge defender K’Lavon Chaisson to a one-year, $11 million contract with $10.3 million guaranteed. Based on last season’s production, those contracts should have been closer together. And Chaisson had a legitimate case to take the lead. In 2025 with the Ravens and Chargers, Oweh had 7.5 sacks and 51 total pressures, while Chaisson had 7.5 sacks and 52 pressures with the AFC champions during the regular season and was a menace in the playoffs. Now, this was Chaisson’s latest turn after an underwhelming four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars, the team that took him with the 20th overall pick out of LSU in the 2020 draft. The Carolina Panthers signed him in March 2024, but he didn’t make final cuts. The Las Vegas Raiders took their shot by signing Chaisson to their practice squad on Sept. 10, promoted him to the active roster on Oct. 5, and were rewarded with Chaisson’s six sacks and 29 pressures — his best NFL season to date. This prompted the Patriots to sign Chaisson to a one-year, $3 million contract, which he more than maxed out . Chaisson was a Secret Superstar at the start and at the end of the 2025 season, because the tape did not lie. In four seasons with the Jaguars, K'Lavon Chaisson did very little to validate his 20th overall selection in the 2020 draft. One season with the Raiders turned things around, and now, the Patriots will look to put the cherry on top. pic.twitter.com/eCODMkKm8H — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) July 14, 2025 Like just about everyone on the @Patriots ' defense, K'Lavon Chaisson has gone from very good to thermonuclear in the postseason. pic.twitter.com/LUoGr2LWiJ — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) January 22, 2026 Putting Chaisson and Oweh on the same defensive line should increase Washington’s pass-rush possibilities to an extreme degree. “Man, just continue to believe,” Chaisson said in his first Commanders press conference, when asked about his specific NFL path. “That’s it. Continue to believe. Everybody’s story is not the same. Everybody’s journey is not the same. “Comparison is the biggest thief of joy. So the best thing I loved about all this is the journey. Everything that I learned, the lessons…
