title: Commanders-Vikings Week 16; can Daronte Jones outdo his mentor Brian Flores?
summary: It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 O’Clock Club The 5 o’clock club is published from time to time during the season, and aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. Feel free to introduce topics that interest you in the comments below. […]
full_text: Dec 7, 2025; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (22) rushes the ball against Minnesota Vikings linebacker Gabriel Murphy (59) during the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images | Brad Rempel-Imagn Images It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 O’Clock Club The 5 o’clock club is published from time to time during the season, and aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. Feel free to introduce topics that interest you in the comments below. CLICK HERE to see the full 5 o’clock club archive 2026 opponent preview series: Wk 1 Eagles | Wk 2 Cowboys | Wk 3 Seahawks | Wk 4 Colts | Wk 5 Giants | Wk 6 49ers | Wk 9 Rams | Wk 11 Bengals | Wk 12 Cardinals | Wk 13 Titans | Wk 14 Texans | Wk 15 Falcons Previewing Washington’s 14 opponents of the ‘26 season — one at a time In 2026, the Commanders will, like every other team in the NFL, play 17 games against 14 opponents. With the amount of roster change that NFL teams undergo annually along with the unusually large number of head coach and coordinator changes in 2026, it seems useful to spend some time to review each of Washington’s regular season opponents. VIKINGS The Commanders complete the trifecta of 2026 games played against teams whose head coaches were once offensive coordinators in Washington by taking on Kevin O’Connell after having gone head-to-head against Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers in Week 6 and Sean McVay’s Rams in Week 9. Week 16 Preview: Washington Commanders at Minnesota Vikings Date: Date & Time TBD Location: US Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota The Vikings had a very successful regular season in 2024, winning 14 games behind Sam Darnold before ultimately losing to the Rams on the opening weekend of the playoffs. It may have been the failure in that playoff game that led to Darnold’s departure to the Seahawks, where he led his team to a Super Bowl championship in February. The Vikings entered the 2025 season with sky-high expectations that did not come to fruition as the team stumbled to a 9-8 regular season 3rd place finish in the NFC North, missing the playoffs. They now find themselves caught between two timelines: trying to win right now with veteran Kyler Murray, who has durability concerns, while simultaneously sheltering a young quarterback, JJ McCarthy, whose developmental timeline may have stalled. "Justin Jefferson should never have a season like the one we saw last year." @minakimes needs to see better QB play from the Vikings this season ✍️ pic.twitter.com/ONFoZppIGW — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) July 10, 2026 The Commanders and Vikings will both enter the 2026 season with memories of magical 2024 seasons that ended in ultimate playoff disappointment followed by more or less forgettable 2025 seasons. The Commanders have re-tooled the coaching staff and are running it back with Jayden Daniels. The Vikings appear to be flailing about a bit at quarterback, but have stood firm with their coaching staff. Dan Patrick wasn’t having any of Kevin O’Connell’s coachspeak on QB1 pic.twitter.com/JAgCXyT0mT — The Coachspeak Index (@CoachspeakIndex) July 10, 2026 By the time the game is played in Week 16, all the questions about these two rosters and coaching staffs are likely to have been answered, but right now, in mid-July, those questions abound. Will this be a matchup between two NFC powerhouses jockeying for better playoff seeding? Will it, rather, be a meaningless game between two teams suffering through another disappointing season? Or will it end up being a painful, one-sided affair akin to last year’s contest, with one team trying to secure a playoff berth while the other team’s fan base is thinking primarily on the game’s effect on draft position? The All-Time Series Numbers Recently Washington heads to Minnesota trying to break a long losing streak on the road. The burgundy & gold has lost four straight games in the Twin Cities, with its last victory there coming back in 2007. Dan Quinn’s roster now faces the challenge of winning inside U.S. Bank Stadium to erase nearly two decades of road struggles against the Vikings. The most recent game (which I referenced in the introduction above) was a 31-0 shellacking put on the Commanders in December 2025. Many fans feel as if Kliff Kingsbury sealed his doom in DC with a series of 3 incomplete passes after the Commanders faced 2nd & goal at the Vikings 2 yard line on Washington’s first possession of the game. Washington turned the ball over to the Vikings just before the end of the 1st quarter, then the defense allowed a 98-yard TD drive to make the game 14-0 and the rout was on. Washington’s subsequent offensive drives comprised 3 punts, 2 interceptions, and a fumble — with Vikings QB JJ McCarthy taking a knee on the final 3 snaps of the game to run off the final 2 minutes in a humiliating Week 14 defeat of Dan Quinn’s team. Historical series Although the Vikings inaugural season was 1961, they didn’t play the Redskins until November 1968. The Vikings got off to a hot start, winning the first two games in the series, and 5 of the first 7 before the Redskins turned things around with 7 straight wins — including a pair of overtime games and 3 playoff victories — from the 1982 postseason to the 1992 postseason. It’s been mostly downhill since that time, however, as the Vikings have won 11 of 15 games played since ‘93, and 8 of 10 since 2010. The Vikings lead the all-time series 16-13, though Washington won 3 of 5 playoff games between the two teams in the 20-year stretch from the ‘73 season to the ‘92 season. Vikings Coaching Staff While there were some staff changes, the Vikings coaching staff returns for the 2026 season substantially the same as it was in 2025, with the same head coach and coordinators. Perhaps the most significant coaching staff change was the hiring of Assistant Head Coach Frank Smith to replace Mike Pettine, who retired. Head Coach : Kevin O’Connell Offensive Coordinator : Wes Phillips Defensive Coordinator : Brian Flores Special Teams Coordinator : Matt Daniels Washington & Minnesota: Contrasting offensive philosophies While Minnesota’s offensive designer — head coach Kevin O’Connell — and Washington’s new OC David Blough are both seen as young, creative and intelligent former players and offensive innovators (and Blough was in Minnesota briefly as a player under KOC), they take different approaches to offensive design. O’Connell, who had a successful 3-year stint in Washington that saw him rise in 3 seasons from QB coach to offensive coordinator, is a direct branch of the dominant Sean McVay coaching tree. His foundational philosophy was cemented while working under Jay Gruden in Washington and later as Sean McVay’s offensive coordinator with the Los Angeles Rams. His system relies heavily on West Coast timing, mid-zone/outside-zone run principles, and a heavy volume of 11-personnel groupings to stress the defense through the air. Like KOC, David Blough has risen rapidly through Washington’s offensive coaching ranks, moving from Assistant QB coach to OC, also in 3 years. While both O’Connell and Blough trace elements of their offensive identity to the same schematic roots, they prioritize entirely different mechanics. Because Blough spent time as a practice squad player directly under O’Connell in Minnesota in 2022, the foundational DNA of the two systems shares a heavy West Coast influence, but his — that is Blough’s — implementation of that system for the 2026 season is expected to differ significantly from that of his old coach. In fact, many people expect his years playing under Ben Johnson in Detroit and working for Kliff Kingsbury in Washington to heavily influence the Washington offensive philosophy, making it a hybrid of multiple successful offensive philosophies. title: David Blough among Washington Commanders with most to prove in 2026
summary: The Commanders are striving to move on quickly from 2025’s 5-12 disaster and show it’s not the start of a troubling trend.   Washington made the NFC title game following the 2024 campaign, a thrilling season where No. 2 overall NFL draft pick Jayden Daniels earned offensive rookie of the year honors. The encore was […]
full_text: The Commanders are striving to move on quickly from 2025’s 5-12 disaster and show it’s not the start of a troubling trend. Washington made the NFC title game following the 2024 campaign, a thrilling season where No. 2 overall NFL draft pick Jayden Daniels earned offensive rookie of the year honors. The encore was a mess, filled with injuries to Daniels, receiver Terry McLaurin, cornerback Trey Amos and others. The defense couldn’t stop anyone and the season ended with a thud that prompted major offseason changes. Washington replaced both coordinators. They invested heavily in creating a younger and faster defense. They worked to surround Daniels with more talent. They largely jettisoned the concept of finding quick veteran fixes on short-term contracts, instead aiming for players on the ascent. If general manager Adam Peters hits on most of his offseason acquisitions, the Commanders will set a proper foundation to support a period of sustained success. Will that happen? We’ll have to wait and see. The entire Commanders organization has something to prove in 2026, from the front office all the way down the roster’s depth chart. That’s why picking three is a virtual impossibility. There’s an argument to be made for so many, and I welcome those in the article comments. We’ll go with three with the most to prove, with players and coaches as options on the table. Offensive coordinator David Blough David Blough has never called offense plays at any level of football. He has never held an NFL coaching position higher than assistant quarterbacks coach. Blough was promoted to Commanders offensive coordinator despite those facts. He has been lauded by those who worked closely with him as a coach and former NFL quarterback, including now Bears head coach Ben Johnson after their time together in Detroit. There’s confidence Blough can get Washington’s offense going with a largely under-center offense that prioritizes a strong rushing game – expect lots of zone concepts – and playaction passing. All that should help protect Daniels and provide elements not offered under previous coordinator Kliff Kingsbury. Blough must show he can do the job well, install his system well and game-plan against the opponent. If he can help Daniels and the Commanders thrive, Washington will be competitive quickly. WR Treylon Burks The Commanders have not added a veteran free-agent receiver this summer, with third-round NFL draft pick as the last big acquisition for a team in clear need of a No. 2 receiver opposite Terry McLaurin. That doesn’t mean they won’t sign someone like Stefon Diggs off the street. They just haven’t to this point. That creates a golden opportunity for former first-round pick Treylon Burks to live up to his draft slot. Injuries have been the biggest roadblock for a player who hasn’t exceeded 444 receiving yards in a season . This is a real prove-it year for a 26-year-old who has flashed brilliance but never established himself as a steady threat. Burks has a chance to earn steady reps if the Commanders stand pat, even if Williams sees significant time. He’ll have to stave off internal competition from Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, so this is a long road to a starting spot. He must earn trust each day and prove he can be that dude. CB Mike Sainristil Mike Sainristil didn’t have a good year in 2025. Neither did the Commanders defense. Sainristil was better as a second-round rookie in 2024. He had a 112.4 passer rating against him last season and a 97.7 the year prior, per NFL Next Gen Stats . Sainristil has his believers – count our Mark Tyler chief among them – and will have a chance to prove them right in 2026. The Commanders also added veteran competition to the room. While Amik Robertson is expected to play a ton in the slot, he, like Sainristil, has inside-out versatility. Rasul Douglas was a late add with tons of starting experience, and surely signed here pushing for an every-down spot. Sainristil has the tools to be an every-down player in this league. This summer and fall, he’ll have to prove that’s the case. QB Jayden Daniels I really struggled with whether to put Daniels on this list, considering there are so many things he doesn’t have to prove to anyone. It’s clear that Daniels is a true franchise quarterback capable of producing among the NFL’s best. He showed that as a rookie in 2024. There’s no doubting his accuracy or arm strength or football IQ. There shouldn’t be consternation about him playing well predominantly under center. He’s a leader. He commands respect. He’s got it. Health is the only thing, after missing 10 games last season due to various injuries . That’s still true after he played 17 plus the playoffs the year before. The only question about him coming out of college was about dealing with the heavy hits his playing style often invites , though he has always been a good pocket passer with solid footwork. Playing a full season would be great for the Commanders and would silence the one question mark about his NFL potential. Honorable mentions HC Dan Quinn: His seat will get mighty warm if the Commanders struggle in 2026. C Nick Allegretti: Center’s an important position in Blough’s offense. Can someone who has primarily been an NFL guard thrive in such a big role? K Jake Moody: The 49ers made Moody a third-round draft pick in 2023, but he has struggled to find consistency in the NFL. The Commanders added Drew Stevens as competition. Will Moody secure his spot and realize potential? LB Frankie Luvu: The linebacker has been really good for a long time, but is coming off a down year. Can he find vintage form under Jones? EDGE Odafe Oweh: He has been really good at times, but generally as a secondary edge rusher. Can he step up and the guy? DL Daron Payne/EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson: Both guys are in contract years and certainly in search of a long-term payday. They must earn such deals with strong seasons.

title: Commanders news: Trey Amos says “healthy” and “good for training camp”
summary: The Daily Slop – 20 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - SEPTEMBER 21: Trey Amos #23 of the Washington Commanders runs off of the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Northwest Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 20 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) NFL players with the most on the line in 2026: One from every team Washington Commanders: Jayden Daniels, QB The real answer is head coach Dan Quinn, who has turned to two first-year coordinators when his future in Washington may depend on a winning season. But this is a players-only list, and although this player is only a year removed from being the NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Year, he inherently faces the most pressure on Washington’s roster. The Commanders haven’t wavered in their belief in Daniels, and he’s given them little reason to do so. But should he have another injury-riddled season or look wholly unlike the player he was in 2024, there undoubtedly will be comparisons to Robert Griffin III or questions about whether he’s the franchise’s long-term answer at QB. But another solid season from Daniels, and especially one with a playoff berth, would reaffirm his place among the league’s top QBs and all but guarantee him a massive second contract. (I’m betting on the latter.) — Nicki Jhabvala To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Commanders training camp primer: Safeties Biggest Training Camp Question : How do Harris & Martin Fit? Harris arrived with positional versatility that could matter with experience at both safety spots and cornerback, though he struggled mightily at free safety after missing at least 10% of his tackles for the third straight season while allowing completions on 60% of targets. A fractured fibula would then end his first season as a Commander after appearing in just nine games, giving him a chance to prove himself once again along the backline. Similar could be said for Martin, who started all but one of Washington’s 17 games in 2025, his third season with the organization, despite battling consistent injuries. His ten missed tackles marked a career-high, yet so did his 154.5 passer rating allowed when targeted — comfortably surpassing the 86.4 rating he allowed as a rookie in 2023. Though he’s amassed four forced fumbles and six pass deflections over the last two seasons, 2025 marked his first season without an interception. Now under a coordinator that has made clear takeaways are a priority, Martin has a chance to prove 2025 was an outlier. Did being less than 100% all season play a role? 2026 can prove that. Martin adds IQ to the backline, but with Jones implementing three safety looks, could Martin also be used in nickel packages with Amik Robertson? The former second round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft will need to showcase that — and consistently. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Six Commanders players who could force tough roster decisions Chris Hilton Jr. – Commanders WR Much has been made about the Commanders’ concerns in their wide receiver room. Speculation remains high about another dependable veteran coming into the fold, but Adam Peters might also decide to stick with what he has and hope one or two of the young hopefuls can break out. That’s risky, but it does have some merit. The competition for places will make everyone better, and though Chris Hilton Jr. has a huge fight to stay relevant, he’s got the athletic scope to enter the roster conversation with a strong camp and preseason. Hilton has a previously established connection with Jayden Daniels from their time together at LSU. His production with the Tigers was modest, which is why he didn’t hear his name called during the 2026 NFL Draft. At the same time, there is also a lot of untapped potential if he can become a more convincing route runner. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN NFL All-Backup Team: Could a roster of bench players contend? Washington Commanders G/OT Andrew Wylie, LB Leo Chenal [Bill-in-Bangkok: Leo Chenal as a backup is a tough sell] Two former Chiefs make it to our team of backups. Wylie is an ideal sixth lineman, a utility player with significant starting experience at guard and tackle. He could start at either right guard or right tackle in a pinch. Chenal will play in base defense for the Commanders, but when they’re in their nickel package, he’ll likely come off the field with Frankie Luvu and Sonny Styles staying on. Chenal was excellent for the Chiefs in their second Super Bowl victory over the 49ers and offers our team sound tackling and some meaningful thump against the run. Miami Dolphins K Zane Gonzalez Let’s get the kicker off the board! The Dolphins are one of the few teams with two veteran kickers on their roster, so Gonzalez is an easy pick for us after hitting 86.4% of his attempts last season in Atlanta. Green Bay Packers CB Benjamin St-Juste The Packers are usually a reliable source for talented depth, but this year, we’re going for one of their free agent additions on a low-cost contract. St-Juste was a promising cornerback in Washington before falling out of the starting lineup in 2024. The Canadian wisely chose to join the Chargers last offseason, where he was one of the many defensive backs to revitalize their careers under Jesse Minter, allowing a 68.3 passer rating in coverage across 356 snaps. Atlanta Falcons WR Olamide Zaccheaus Zaccheaus is an ideal third wide receiver. Yes, 2025 wasn’t his most productive season in terms of yardage, but the well-traveled veteran is one of the league’s best blocking wide receivers and is effective just enough as a pass catcher to justify staying on the field. With the Falcons likely living in 12 personnel in 2026, Zaccheaus will be playing behind Jahan Dotson across from Drake London this season. Don’t be surprised if he is moved ahead of Dotson by the time the season ends. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN NFL players love wearing their ‘slippers and slides, baby!’ THERE ARE TWO kinds of slipper wearers in the NFL. Those who wear normal slippers and those who … don’t. Washington Commanders defensive end Javontae Jean-Baptiste is definitely among the latter, because his latest choice was a pair of purple bear claw mules, which he purchased last season for $115 from Bravest Studios. View Link They’re not his only pair. “My first pair was brown, like a grizzly bear,” explains Jean-Baptiste, who said he ordered a pair of blue bear claw mules last season for teammate Dante Fowler Jr . “Then I saw the purple, and it’s my favorite color, so I got that. … They’re comfortable.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Podcasts & videos THE NEWS EVERYONE WANTED: Trey Amos HEALTHY for Commanders Training Camp + Cornerback Discussion When I asked him, “Are you healthy?” He said, “We’re going to be healthy and we’re going to be good for training camp,” which, again, starts in 10 days. So, this is not like a long-term projection thing. Either he’s feeling healthy or he’s not. And he said that he is. If Dan Quinn says, “Trey, we’re going to ease you back into it; you’re not a full participant, but you will be out here doing some drills,” that’s one thing. So, I’m not guaranteeing that he will be a full participant. I’m not guaranteeing that he’ll be playing in joint practices and stuff like that. But, from the horse’s mouth itself, he is healthy. This is huge because Trey did not practice with the team during OTAAS and during mini camp. title: Why the Washington Commanders drafted QB Athan Kaliakmanis
summary: This article will not take a deeper look at Athan Kaliakmanis’ nicknames, of which there are several, including “the Greek Rifle” and “Golden Boy.” Instead, we will focus on what makes the selection of the former Rutgers QB in the seventh round a good decision. Following the conclusion of the 2026 NFL draft, there were […]
full_text: Nov 29, 2025; Piscataway, New Jersey, USA; Rutgers Scarlet Knights quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis (16) fights for yards as Penn State Nittany Lions cornerback Zion Tracy (7) tackles during the second half at SHI Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images This article will not take a deeper look at Athan Kaliakmanis’ nicknames, of which there are several, including “the Greek Rifle” and “Golden Boy.” Instead, we will focus on what makes the selection of the former Rutgers QB in the seventh round a good decision. Following the conclusion of the 2026 NFL draft, there were several analysts that disagreed with this premise, assigning Adam Peters’ final pick an overall “C-” grade. 2026 NFL Draft grades for every NFC East team 🧵 📊 Commanders: A+ LB Sonny Styles (7): A WR Antonio Williams (71): A+ EDGE Joshua Josephs (147): A+ RB Kaytron Allen (187): B+ C Matt Gulbin (209): B+ QB Athan Kaliakmanis (223): C- pic.twitter.com/g75smXtakK — Pro Football Network (@PFN365) May 7, 2026 My Commanders draft grades: Round 1 (7): Sonny Styles – A+ Round 3 (71): Antonio Williams B Round 5 (147): Joshua Josephs A Round 6 (187): RB Kaytron Allen B+ Round 6 (209): Matt Gulbin B Round 7 (223): Athan Kaliakmanis C- — Tiller56 (@Tiller56) April 25, 2026 Reasons for the poor grade varied, but most of the criticism centered around a perceived lack of need, the opinion that there were better options still available, and that Kaliakmanis’ overall body of work in college was not impressive. Let’s address each item separately. The need at the position might not be readily apparent to some as Marcus Mariota returns for a third season to back up Jayden Daniels. Generally viewed as one of the better QB2s in the league, Mariota has seen far more game action than most would prefer. In the first season, Marcus proved his worth early, taking over for an injured Daniels in the team’s matchup versus the Carolina Panthers and skillfully leading the team to a 40-7 victory. More importantly, he came into the last game of the season to guide the team in a comeback win versus the Cowboys and clinched the 6th seed in the NFC playoffs for the Commanders with a last-second throw to Terry McLaurin. Things started to unravel when Mariota was pressed into service the second half of last season, starting eight games with a 2-6 win-loss record. While the team had already been decimated by injuries by the time Mariota started the majority of his games, his play slowly deteriorated over the course of the season, and Marcus’ decision-making in London’s Miami game was questionable. Turning 33 years old in October and still commanding one of the highest backup quarterback salaries in the league, Washington may look to go in another direction in 2027. While another veteran is always an option, a younger player with potential to grow along with David Blough would be preferable. The Commanders coaching staff signaled that Sam Hartman was not that player when they opted to go with Josh Johnson at the end of the season. So what makes Athan the choice over other options that were available at the tail end of the draft, including Garrett Nussmeier or Haynes King? Kaliakmanis doesn’t distinguish himself in the size or athleticism categories, with okay to good ratings in most categories and a poor one for speed. Athan Kaliakmanis was drafted in round 7 with pick 223 in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 5.37 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 523 out of 1128 QB from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/i2lhw1snUY pic.twitter.com/mEnHvsNTmG — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 25, 2026 Athan certainly doesn’t have the mobility of a Haynes King ( RAS 9.61 ) or the arm of Nussmeier, and his performance under pressure is a work in progress. He does have demonstrated rhythm and timing with a quick release along with the ability to challenge all three levels of defense, which makes him a good fit for David Blough’s proposed offense. The arm strength might not be elite, but Kaliakmanis throws an extremely accurate deep ball with a nice trajectory to match his wide receivers downfield. Athan Kaliakmanis is one of the best QBs in the country pic.twitter.com/GfVtVPsQgC — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 23, 2025 Can’t wait to watch Athan KaliakManis play again pic.twitter.com/M3NmAI1USV — CFBTalkDaily (@CFBTalkDaily) May 15, 2025 His accuracy is inconsistent, as is his ball placement, so what made the Washington Commanders invest a draft pick in him over other options? Potential. Specifically, potential at the most important position in the game. Athan doesn’t have the college resume of a Garret Nussmeier or the playmaking ability of Haynes King, but what he does have is untapped potential. Kaliakmanis wasn’t even a starter at Minnesota until his third year in college, but he demonstrated a decidedly linear progression after transferring to Rutgers. His decision-making, production, and even his arm strength increased exponentially. Athan’s completion rate jumped from 53.9% in 2024 to 62.2% in 2025, a significant leap that coincided with 20 touchdowns against only seven interceptions. His PFSN College QB Impact score has increased every season, resulting in a career-high 82.2 score in his final campaign. The intangibles are there as well. Kaliakmanis has a high football IQ and understanding of the game and called his own pass protections on the field. He has the ability to go through full-field progressions if given the necessary time. Athan is considered a plus culture fit, and the Commanders decided to bring him in for a Top 30 visit . That is where he sold the staff on his intangibles, coachability, and potential upside. In fact, he was the team’s third three-voter caucus pick by the Commanders’ war room. There was enough there that, with Kaliakmanis visiting six teams in the last eight days before the draft, the team decided not to risk losing him in the scrum for undrafted free agents. Why did the Washington Commanders draft Athan Kaliakmanis? As Adam Peters explained to him following the selection, the quarterback had convinced them there was no other choice.
